executive_summary:
Nigeria's real estate market is witnessing significant developments, particularly in the areas of mortgage financing and diaspora investment. The Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) is set to launch a Diaspora National Housing Fund (NHF) Mortgage Loan on August 7, 2026, targeting eligible Nigerians living and working abroad. This move is expected to boost diaspora investment in the Nigerian real estate sector. Additionally, the performance of Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) in Nigeria has been impressive, with some REITs returning over 35% year-to-date as of end-June 2026.

The Nigerian real estate market is also experiencing growth in the luxury segment, with Ikoyi luxury pricing surpassing ₦1.1 billion threshold. Furthermore, the Lekki-Epe Expressway corridor is seeing a surge in premium residential delivery, with several high-end projects underway. The government's efforts to address the housing deficit, including the launch of the 'Renewed Hope' plan and the One Million Homes Housing Project, are also expected to impact the market.

The diaspora market is a key area of focus, with over $90 billion in diaspora remittances between 2020 and 2024, growing at a rate of 9% YoY. The 'Own It 4 Sure' initiative is aimed at converting a larger share of this flow into documented real estate assets. The performance of Newmark Hotels, the hospitality management partner, and the rental pool's actual monthly disbursement performance will also be crucial in determining the success of the rental-pool value proposition.

In conclusion, the Nigerian real estate market is experiencing significant developments, driven by government initiatives, diaspora investment, and growth in the luxury segment. The market is expected to continue growing, driven by the increasing demand for housing and the government's efforts to address the housing deficit.
